sentences.zh: 太宗諸子

translations.literal: Sons of Taizong
translations.idiomatic: The Sons of Emperor Taizong

sentences.zh: 太宗子十四人：蒲魯虎、胡魯、斛魯補、阿魯帶、阿魯補、斛沙虎、阿鄰、阿魯、鶻懶、胡里甲、神土門、斛孛束、斡烈、鶻沙。

translations.literal: Taizong had fourteen sons: Puluhu, Hulu, Hulubu, Aludai, Alubu, Hushahu, Alin, Alu, Gulian, Hulijia, Shentumen, Hubosu, Wolie, and Gusha.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong fathered fourteen sons: Puluhu, Hulu, Hulubu, Aludai, Alubu, Hushahu, Alin, Alu, Gulian, Hulijia, Shentumen, Hubosu, Wolie, and Gusha.

sentences.zh: 宗磐本名蒲魯虎。

translations.literal: Zong Pan's original name was Puluhu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Pan was born Puluhu.

sentences.zh: 天輔五年，都統杲取中京，宗磐與斡魯、宗翰宗幹皆為之副。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu, Commander-in-Chief Gao took the Central Capital; Zong Pan, Wolu, Zong Han, and Zong Gan all served as his deputies.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 5 Commander-in-Chief Gao took the Central Capital. Zong Pan, Wolu, Zong Han, and Zong Gan all served as his deputies.

sentences.zh: 天會十年，為國論忽魯勃極烈。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Tianhui he became guolun hulu bojilie.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 10 he became guolun hulu bojilie.

sentences.zh: 熙宗即位，為尚書令，封宋國王。

translations.literal: When Xizong took the throne, he was made Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong took the throne, he was made director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜太師，與宗幹、宗翰並領三省事。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Preceptor and together with Zong Gan and Zong Han jointly headed the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed grand preceptor and, together with Zong Gan and Zong Han, jointly headed the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 熙宗優禮宗室，宗翰沒後，宗磐日益跋扈。

translations.literal: Xizong treated the imperial clan generously; after Zong Han died, Zong Pan daily grew more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong showed the imperial clan generous favor. After Zong Han's death, Zong Pan grew increasingly arrogant and domineering.

sentences.zh: 嘗與宗幹爭論於上前，即上表求退。

translations.literal: He once argued with Zong Gan before the emperor and at once memorialized requesting to retire.
translations.idiomatic: He once quarreled with Zong Gan in the emperor's presence and immediately submitted a memorial asking to withdraw from office.

sentences.zh: 烏野奏曰：「陛下富於春秋，而大臣不協，恐非國家之福。」

translations.literal: Wuye memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty is in the prime of life, yet the great ministers are not in accord—this may not be a blessing to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Wuye submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty is still young, yet your chief ministers are at odds. That bodes ill for the realm."

sentences.zh: 熙宗因為兩解。

translations.literal: Xizong thereupon reconciled the two.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then mediated between them.

sentences.zh: 宗磐愈驕恣。

translations.literal: Zong Pan became all the more proud and insolent.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Pan grew only more arrogant and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 其後于熙宗前持馬向宗幹，都點檢蕭仲恭呵止之。

translations.literal: Later, in Xizong's presence he brandished a whip toward Zong Gan, and the Chief Inspector Xiao Zhonggong shouted him down and stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: Later, before the emperor he raised his riding crop against Zong Gan; the chief inspector Xiao Zhonggong rebuked him and made him stop.

sentences.zh: 既而左副元帥撻懶、東京留守宗雋入朝，宗磐陰相黨與，而宗雋遂為右丞相，用事。

translations.literal: Before long the Left Deputy Commander-in-Chief Tadan and the Eastern Capital prefect Zong Jun came to court; Zong Pan secretly formed a faction with them, and Zong Jun then became Right Chancellor and wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the left deputy commander-in-chief Tadan and the Eastern Capital prefect Zong Jun arrived at court. Zong Pan formed a secret clique with them, and Zong Jun became right chancellor and dominated affairs.

sentences.zh: 撻懶屬尊，功多，先薦劉豫，立為齊帝，至是唱議以河南、陝西與宋，使稱臣。

translations.literal: Tadan was of honored lineage with many achievements; he had earlier recommended Liu Yu and installed him as Emperor of Qi; now he advocated returning Henan and Shaanxi to Song and making them acknowledge vassalage.
translations.idiomatic: Tadan came from an exalted line and had great merit to his credit. He had earlier backed Liu Yu as emperor of Qi; now he urged returning Henan and Shaanxi to the Song and making them submit as vassals.

sentences.zh: 熙宗命群臣議，宗室大臣言其不可。

translations.literal: Xizong ordered the ministers to deliberate; the imperial-clan grandees said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong ordered a full deliberation. The senior imperial clansmen declared the plan unacceptable.

sentences.zh: 宗磐、宗雋助之，卒以與宋。

translations.literal: Zong Pan and Zong Jun supported it, and in the end the territories were given to Song.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Pan and Zong Jun pressed the proposal, and the lands were at last returned to Song.

sentences.zh: 其後宗磐、宗雋、撻懶謀作亂，宗幹、希尹發其事，熙宗下詔誅之。

translations.literal: Afterward Zong Pan, Zong Jun, and Tadan plotted rebellion; Zong Gan and Xiyin exposed the affair, and Xizong issued an edict executing them.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zong Pan, Zong Jun, and Tadan conspired to rebel. Zong Gan and Xiyin exposed the plot, and the emperor ordered their execution.

sentences.zh: 坐與宴飲者，皆貶削決責有差。

translations.literal: Those who had shared in their banquets were all demoted, reduced, and sentenced to varying penalties.
translations.idiomatic: Those who had attended their feasts were all demoted and punished according to their degree of involvement.

sentences.zh: 赦其弟斛魯補等九人，並赦撻懶，出為行台左丞相。

translations.literal: He pardoned nine others including his younger brother Hulubu, and also pardoned Tadan, sending him out as left chancellor of the branch secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He pardoned nine others, including his younger brother Hulubu, and even pardoned Tadan, appointing him left chancellor of the regional secretariat.

sentences.zh: 皇后生日，宰相諸王妃主命婦入賀。

translations.literal: On the empress's birthday, the chancellors, royal consorts, princesses, and titled ladies entered to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the empress's birthday the chancellors, royal consorts, princesses, and court ladies came to offer their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 熙宗命去樂，曰：「宗磐等皆近屬，輒構逆謀，情不能樂也。」

translations.literal: Xizong ordered the music removed, saying: "Zong Pan and the others are all close kin who rashly plotted treason—I cannot take pleasure in this."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong ordered the music stopped, saying, "Zong Pan and the others were close kin who nevertheless plotted rebellion. I cannot take pleasure in this celebration."

sentences.zh: 以黃金合及兩銀鼎獻明德宮太皇太后，並以金合、銀鼎賜宗幹、希尹焉。

translations.literal: He presented a gold box and two silver cauldrons to the Grand Empress Dowager of the Mingde Palace, and also bestowed gold boxes and silver cauldrons on Zong Gan and Xiyin.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a gold casket and two silver vessels to the Grand Empress Dowager at Mingde Palace, and bestowed matching gold caskets and silver vessels on Zong Gan and Xiyin as well.

sentences.zh: 宗固本名胡魯。

translations.literal: Zong Gu's original name was Hulu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Gu was born Hulu.

sentences.zh: 天會十五年為燕京留守，封豳王。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianhui he was made Yanjing regent and enfeoffed as Prince of Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianhui 15 he was made Yanjing regent and enfeoffed as Prince of Bin.

sentences.zh: 宗雅本名斛魯補，封代王。

translations.literal: Zong Ya's original name was Hulubu; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ya, born Hulubu, was enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 宗偉本名阿魯補，封虞王。

translations.literal: Zong Wei's original name was Alubu; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Wei, born Alubu, was enfeoffed as Prince of Yu.

sentences.zh: 宗英本名斛沙虎，封滕王。

translations.literal: Zong Ying's original name was Hushahu; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ying, born Hushahu, was enfeoffed as Prince of Teng.

sentences.zh: 宗懿本名阿鄰，封薛王。

translations.literal: Zong Yi's original name was Alin; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Yi, born Alin, was enfeoffed as Prince of Xue.

sentences.zh: 宗本本名阿魯，封厚王。

translations.literal: Zong Ben's original name was Alu; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Hou.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ben, born Alu, was enfeoffed as Prince of Hou.

sentences.zh: 鶻懶封翼王。

translations.literal: Gulian was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Gulian was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 宗美本名胡里甲，封豐王。

translations.literal: Zong Mei's original name was Hulijia; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Mei, born Hulijia, was enfeoffed as Prince of Feng.

sentences.zh: 神土門封鄆王。

translations.literal: Shentumen was enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Shentumen was enfeoffed as Prince of Yun.

sentences.zh: 斛孛束封霍王。

translations.literal: Hubosu was enfeoffed as Prince of Huo.
translations.idiomatic: Hubosu was enfeoffed as Prince of Huo.

sentences.zh: 斡烈封蔡王。

translations.literal: Wolie was enfeoffed as Prince of Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Wolie was enfeoffed as Prince of Cai.

sentences.zh: 宗哲本名鶻沙，封畢王。

translations.literal: Zong Zhe's original name was Gusha; he was enfeoffed as Prince of Bi.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Zhe, born Gusha, was enfeoffed as Prince of Bi.

sentences.zh: 皆天眷元年受封。

translations.literal: All received their enfeoffments in the first year of Tianjuan.
translations.idiomatic: All received their enfeoffments in Tianjuan 1.

sentences.zh: 宗順本名阿魯帶，天會二年薨，皇統五年贈金紫光祿大夫，後封徐王。

translations.literal: Zong Shun's original name was Aludai; he died in the second year of Tianhui, was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purple Tassel in the fifth year of Huangtong, and later enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Shun, born Aludai, died in Tianhui 2. In Huangtong 5 he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purple Tassel and later enfeoffed as Prince of Xu.

sentences.zh: 宗磐既誅，熙宗使宗固子京往燕京慰諭宗固。

translations.literal: After Zong Pan was executed, Xizong sent Zong Gu's son Jing to Yanjing to console and reassure Zong Gu.
translations.idiomatic: After Zong Pan was executed, Xizong sent Zong Gu's son Jing to Yanjing to console and reassure Zong Gu.

sentences.zh: 既而翼王鶻懶複與行台左丞相撻懶謀反伏誅。

translations.literal: Before long Prince of Yi Gulian again conspired with the regional commissioner's left chancellor Tadan to rebel and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Prince of Yi Gulian again conspired with Regional Commissioner Left Chancellor Tadan to rebel and was executed.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「燕京留守豳王宗固等或謂當絕屬籍，朕所不忍。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Yanjing regent Prince of Bin Zong Gu and the others—some say their clan registers should be cut off; I cannot bear it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared, "Yanjing regent Prince of Bin Zong Gu and the others—some say their clan registers should be cut off. I cannot bear that.

sentences.zh: 宗固等但不得稱皇叔，其母妻封號從而降者，審依舊典。」

translations.literal: Zong Gu and the others simply may not be called imperial uncles; as for their mothers' and wives' titles and ranks, those reduced in accordance with precedent shall be examined according to the old regulations."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Gu and the others simply may not be called imperial uncles. As for their mothers' and wives' titles and ranks, those reduced in accordance with precedent shall be examined according to the old regulations."

sentences.zh: 皇統二年，複封宗雅為代王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangtong, Zong Ya was again enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 2 Zong Ya was again enfeoffed as Prince of Dai.

sentences.zh: 宗固為判大宗正，六年，為太保、右丞相兼中書令。

translations.literal: Zong Gu served as director of the Great Clan Court; in the sixth year he became Grand Guardian, right chancellor, and concurrently director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Gu served as director of the Great Clan Court. In the sixth year he became grand guardian, right chancellor, and concurrently director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 是歲，薨。

translations.literal: That year he died.
translations.idiomatic: That year he died.

sentences.zh: 海陵在熙宗時，見太宗諸子勢強，而宗磐尤跋扈，與鶻懶相繼皆以逆誅，心忌之。

translations.literal: During Xizong's reign Hailing saw that Taizong's sons were powerful, and Zong Pan especially overbearing; Gulian too was executed for treason in succession, and he harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: While Xizong still reigned, Prince Hailing saw how strong Taizong's sons had become—Zong Pan above all was domineering, and Gulian was soon executed for treason as well—and he came to resent them.

sentences.zh: 熙宗厚於宗室，禮遇不衰。

translations.literal: Xizong was generous toward the imperial clan, and his courtesy never waned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong continued to treat the imperial clan with unstinting generosity and respect.

sentences.zh: 海陵嘗與秉德、唐括辯私議，主上不宜寵遇太宗諸子太甚。

translations.literal: Hailing once privately discussed with Bingde and Tangutuo Bian that the sovereign ought not favor Taizong's sons too greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing once confided to Bingde and Tangutuo Bian that the throne should not indulge Taizong's sons too lavishly.

sentences.zh: 及篡立，謁奠太廟。

translations.literal: When he usurped the throne, he performed obeisance at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: After seizing the throne he went to pay his respects at the imperial ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 韓王亨素號材武，使攝右衛將軍，密諭之曰：「爾勿以此職為輕，朕疑太宗諸子太強，得卿衛左右，可無慮耳。」

translations.literal: Prince Han Gongheng was known for martial talent; Hailing had him act as acting commander of the Right Guard and secretly instructed him: "Do not take this post lightly. I suspect Taizong's sons are too strong; with you guarding my side I need have no worry."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Han Gongheng was famed for martial prowess. Hailing appointed him acting commander of the Right Guard and told him privately, "Do not treat this post lightly. I fear Taizong's sons are too powerful; with you at my side I shall have nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 遂與秘書監蕭裕謀去宗本兄弟。

translations.literal: He then plotted with the Secretariat Director Xiao Yu to eliminate Zong Ben and his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He then conspired with Secretariat Director Xiao Yu to destroy Zong Ben and his brothers.

sentences.zh: 太宗子孫於是焉盡，語在《宗本傳》中。

translations.literal: Taizong's descendants were thus extinguished; the account is in the "Biography of Zong Ben."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's line was wiped out in this way; the full account appears in the "Biography of Zong Ben."

sentences.zh: 宗本本名阿魯。

translations.literal: Zong Ben's original name was Alu.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ben was born Alu.

sentences.zh: 皇統九年，為右丞相兼中書令，進太保，鄰三省事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Huangtong he became Right Chancellor and concurrently Director of the Secretariat, was promoted to Grand Guardian, and oversaw the three secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangtong 9 he was appointed right chancellor and director of the Secretariat, promoted to grand guardian, and put in charge of all three secretariats.

sentences.zh: 海陵篡立，進太傅，領三省事。

translations.literal: When Hailing usurped the throne, Zong Ben was promoted to Grand Tutor and headed the three secretariats.
translations.idiomatic: After Hailing's coup he was made grand tutor and retained control of the three secretariats.

sentences.zh: 初，宗幹謀誅宗磐，故海陵心忌太宗諸子。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Zong Gan had plotted to kill Zong Pan, Hailing resented Taizong's sons.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had long resented Taizong's sons, not least because Zong Gan had once plotted to kill Zong Pan.

sentences.zh: 熙宗時，海陵私議宗本等勢強，主上不宜優寵太甚。

translations.literal: During Xizong's reign Hailing had privately said that Zong Ben and the others were too powerful and the sovereign should not favor them excessively.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xizong he had already complained that men like Zong Ben were too powerful and that the throne was indulging them too far.

sentences.zh: 及篡立，猜忌益深，遂與秘書監蕭裕謀殺太宗諸子。

translations.literal: After usurping the throne his suspicion deepened, and he plotted with Secretariat Director Xiao Yu to kill Taizong's sons.
translations.idiomatic: Once he seized power his suspicion only deepened, and he joined Secretariat Director Xiao Yu in a plot to exterminate Taizong's sons.

sentences.zh: 誣以秉德出領行台，與宗本別，因會飲，約內外相應。

translations.literal: He framed the affair by having Bingde go out to head the branch secretariat and part from Zong Ben; at a farewell feast they agreed on coordinated action inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: He set the trap by sending Bingde out to head the regional secretariat and taking leave of Zong Ben at a parting feast, where they supposedly agreed on coordinated action inside and outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 使尚書省令史蕭玉告宗本親謂玉言：「以汝於我故舊，必無它意，可布腹心事。

translations.literal: He had the Ministry of Rites clerk Xiao Yu report that Zong Ben had personally told Yu: "Because you and I are old friends, you surely have no other intent—speak your inmost thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: He had Ministry of Rites clerk Xiao Yu claim that Zong Ben had told him in person, "You and I are old friends, so you must have no hidden purpose—lay bare what is in your heart.

sentences.zh: 鄰省臨行，言彼在外諭說軍民，無以外患為慮。

translations.literal: When the neighboring chancellor was about to depart, he said that out there he would rally troops and civilians and that there was no need to worry about external threats.
translations.idiomatic: When the neighboring chancellor was leaving, he said that abroad he would rally troops and the people and that there was no need to fear outside enemies.

sentences.zh: 若太傅為內應，何事不成。」

translations.literal: If the Grand Tutor acts as inner ally, what affair could fail?"
translations.idiomatic: If the Grand Tutor serves as our ally within the capital, what could we not accomplish?"

sentences.zh: 又雲：「長子鎖里虎當大貴，因是不令見主上。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The eldest son Suolihu is destined for greatness, which is why he is not allowed to see the sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "My eldest son Suolihu is fated for greatness, which is why I do not let him appear before the throne."

sentences.zh: 宗本又言：「左丞相于我及我妃處，稱主上近日見之輒不喜，故心常恐懼，若太傅一日得大位，此心方安。」

translations.literal: Zong Ben also said: "The Left Chancellor, speaking to me and my consort, said the sovereign has lately been displeased whenever he sees us, so I live in constant fear; if the Grand Tutor one day gains the great position, only then will this heart be at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ben also said, "The left chancellor told me and my consort that the sovereign has lately been displeased whenever he sees us, so we live in constant dread; if the Grand Tutor should one day take the throne, only then would our hearts be at ease."

sentences.zh: 唐括辯謂宗本言：「內侍張彥善相，相太傅有天子分。」

translations.literal: Tangutuo Bian told Zong Ben: "The inner attendant Zhang Yan is skilled at physiognomy and reads the Grand Tutor as having the countenance of a Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Tangutuo Bian told Zong Ben, "The inner attendant Zhang Yan reads faces well and says the Grand Tutor has the bearing of a Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 宗本答曰：「宗本有兄東京留守在，宗本何能為是。」

translations.literal: Zong Ben replied: "Zong Ben has an elder brother, the Eastern Capital prefect, still in office—how could Zong Ben do such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ben answered, "I have an elder brother serving as Eastern Capital prefect—how could I do such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 時宗美言「太傅正是太宗主家子，秪太傅便合為北京留守。」

translations.literal: At the time Zong Mei said, "The Grand Tutor is precisely the main-line son of Taizong; only the Grand Tutor ought to be Eastern Capital prefect."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Mei then said, "The Grand Tutor is the legitimate main-line son of Taizong; he alone ought to hold the Eastern Capital."

sentences.zh: 卞臨行與宗本言「事不可遲」。

translations.literal: As Bian was about to depart he told Zong Ben, "The matter must not be delayed."
translations.idiomatic: As Bian was leaving he told Zong Ben, "There must be no delay."

sentences.zh: 宗本與玉言「大計只於日近圍場內予決」。

translations.literal: Zong Ben told Yu, "The great plan will be settled only within the hunting park in the next few days."
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ben told Yu, "The decisive move will be made within the hunting park in the next few days."

sentences.zh: 宗本因以馬一匹、袍一領與玉，充表識物。

translations.literal: Zong Ben therefore gave Yu one horse and one robe as identifying tokens.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ben gave Yu a horse and a robe as tokens of recognition.

sentences.zh: 玉恐圍場日近，身縻於外，不能親奏，遂以告秘書監蕭裕。

translations.literal: Yu feared that as the hunting day drew near he would be tied up outside and unable to report in person, so he told Secretariat Director Xiao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that when the hunt drew near he would be detained outside and unable to report in person, Yu told Secretariat Director Xiao Yu.

sentences.zh: 裕具以聞。

translations.literal: Yu reported the full account.
translations.idiomatic: Yu laid the whole matter before him.

sentences.zh: 蕭玉

translations.literal: Xiao Yu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu

translations.literal: (appendix)
translations.idiomatic: (appendix)

sentences.zh: 蕭玉出入宗本家，親信如家人。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu went in and out of Zong Ben's household and was trusted like a family member.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu frequented Zong Ben's household and was trusted as one of the family.

sentences.zh: 海陵既與蕭裕謀殺宗本、秉德，詔天下，恐天下以宗本、秉德輦皆懿親大臣，本無反狀，裕構成其事，而蕭玉與宗本厚，人所共知，使玉上變，庶可示信。

translations.literal: After Hailing and Xiao Yu had plotted to kill Zong Ben and Bingde, he issued an edict to the realm, fearing the realm would think that Zong Ben and Bingde, both close imperial kin and great ministers, had shown no sign of rebellion and that Yu had fabricated the case; because Xiao Yu was known to all as close to Zong Ben, he had Yu lodge the accusation so credibility might be shown.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hailing and Xiao Yu had plotted the deaths of Zong Ben and Bingde, he proclaimed the case throughout the realm. He feared people would say that these imperial kinsmen and grand ministers had shown no sign of rebellion and that Xiao Yu had fabricated the charges; because everyone knew how close Yu was to Zong Ben, he had Yu lodge the accusation so the story would seem credible.

sentences.zh: 於是使人召宗本等擊鞠，海陵先登樓，命左衛將軍徒單特思及蕭裕妹婿近侍局副使耶律辟離刺小底密伺宗本及判大宗正事宗美，至，即殺之。

translations.literal: He then sent men to summon Zong Ben and the others to play cuju; Hailing went up to a tower first and ordered the Left Guard general Tudan Tesi and Xiao Yu's brother-in-law, Deputy Commissioner of the Inner Service Yelü Pili, to watch Zong Ben and the Director of the Imperial Clan Zong Mei in secret; when they arrived, they were killed at once.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Zong Ben and the others to a cuju match, went up a tower first, and ordered Left Guard general Tudan Tesi and Xiao Yu's brother-in-law, deputy commissioner of the inner service Yelü Pili, to watch Zong Ben and the director of the imperial clan Zong Mei; when they arrived they were killed on the spot.

sentences.zh: 宗美本名胡里甲，臨死神色不變。

translations.literal: Zong Mei's original name was Hulijia; facing death his expression did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Mei, born Hulijia, did not change expression even at the moment of death.

sentences.zh: 宗本已死，蕭裕使人召蕭玉。

translations.literal: After Zong Ben was dead, Xiao Yu sent men to summon Xiao Yu.
translations.idiomatic: After Zong Ben was dead, Xiao Yu sent men to summon the other Xiao Yu.

sentences.zh: 是日，玉送客出城，醉酒，露發披衣，以車載至裕弟點檢蕭祚家。

translations.literal: That day Yu was seeing guests out of the city, drunk; with hair loose and clothes disheveled he was carried by cart to the home of Yu's brother-in-law, Inspector Xiao Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: That day the clerk Yu was escorting guests out of the city, dead drunk, hair loose and clothes awry, and was carted to Inspector Xiao Zuo's house, the brother-in-law of Secretariat Director Xiao Yu.

sentences.zh: 逮日暮，玉酒醒，見軍士圍守之，意為人所累得罪，故至此。

translations.literal: When evening came Yu sobered up and saw soldiers surrounding him; he thought he had been implicated in someone's crime and brought here for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: By evening he had sobered and saw soldiers surrounding him; he assumed he had been dragged into someone else's crime.

sentences.zh: 以頭觸屋壁，號咷曰：「臣未嘗犯罪，老母年七十，願哀憐之。」

translations.literal: He beat his head against the wall and wailed: "Your servant has never committed a crime; my old mother is seventy—please show pity."
translations.idiomatic: He struck his head against the wall and wailed, "I have never committed a crime! My mother is seventy—have mercy on her!"

sentences.zh: 裕附耳告之曰：「主上以宗本諸人不可留，已誅之矣，欲加以反罪，令汝主告其事。

translations.literal: Yu whispered in his ear: "The sovereign decided that Zong Ben and the others could not be left alive and has already executed them; he wishes to add a charge of rebellion and wants you to lodge the accusation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu whispered in his ear, "The sovereign decided Zong Ben and his party could not be allowed to live and has already killed them. He wants to charge them with rebellion and needs you to lodge the accusation.

sentences.zh: 今書汝告款已具，上即問汝，汝但言宗本輩反如狀，勿複異詞，恐禍及汝家也。」

translations.literal: The written accusation is already prepared; when the sovereign questions you, speak only that Zong Ben and his party rebelled as described—do not change your words, lest disaster reach your household."
translations.idiomatic: Your written deposition is already prepared. When the sovereign questions you, say only that Zong Ben and his party rebelled as described—do not contradict it, or your whole household will suffer."

sentences.zh: 裕乃以巾服與玉，引見海陵。

translations.literal: Yu then gave him cap and robes and led him in to see Hailing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu gave him proper cap and robes and led him before Hailing.

sentences.zh: 海陵問玉。

translations.literal: Hailing questioned Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing questioned him.

sentences.zh: 玉言宗本反，具如裕所教。

translations.literal: Yu said Zong Ben had rebelled, exactly as Yu had coached him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu declared that Zong Ben had rebelled, exactly as he had been coached.

sentences.zh: 海陵遺使殺東京留守宗懿、北京留守卞。

translations.literal: Hailing sent envoys to kill the Eastern Capital prefect Zong Yi and the Northern Capital prefect Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing sent envoys to kill the Eastern Capital prefect Zong Yi and the Northern Capital prefect Bian.

sentences.zh: 及遷益都尹畢王宗哲、平陽尹稟、左宣徽使京等，家屬分置別所，止聽各以奴婢五人自隨。

translations.literal: He also transferred Prince Zong Zhe, prefect of Yidu, Bing, the Left Palace Commissioner Jing, and others; their families were placed in separate quarters and each was allowed only five slave attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He also recalled Prince Zong Zhe as prefect of Yidu, Bing, Left Palace Commissioner Jing, and others; their families were confined separately and each man was allowed only five attendants.

sentences.zh: 既而使人要之于路，並其子男無少長皆殺之。

translations.literal: Before long he had men intercept them on the road and killed all their sons, without regard to age.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he had them waylaid on the road and killed every male in their households, young and old alike.

sentences.zh: 而中京留守宗雅喜事佛，世稱「善大王」，海陵知其無能，將存之以奉太宗。

translations.literal: The Central Capital prefect Zong Ya delighted in Buddhism and was known in the world as the "Good Prince"; Hailing knew he was incapable and intended to keep him alive to honor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Central Capital prefect Zong Ya was devoted to Buddhism and known as the "Good Prince." Hailing judged him harmless and meant to spare him to honor Taizong's memory.

sentences.zh: 後召至關，不數日，竟殺之。

translations.literal: Later he summoned him to the pass; within a few days he killed him after all.
translations.idiomatic: Later he summoned him to Tong Pass; within days he killed him anyway.

sentences.zh: 太宗子孫死者七十余人，太宗後遂絕。

translations.literal: More than seventy of Taizong's descendants died; Taizong's line was thus extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: More than seventy of Taizong's descendants perished, and his line was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 卞本名可喜。

translations.literal: Bian's original name was Kexi.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was born Kexi.

sentences.zh: 稟本名胡離改。

translations.literal: Bing's original name was Hugai.
translations.idiomatic: Bing was born Hugai.

sentences.zh: 京，宗固子，本名胡石賚。

translations.literal: Jing, son of Zong Gu, original name Hushai.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, a son of Zong Gu, was born Hushai.

sentences.zh: 蕭玉既如蕭裕教對海陵，海陵遂以宗本、秉德等罪詔天下，以玉上變實之。

translations.literal: After Xiao Yu answered Hailing as Xiao Yu had coached, Hailing issued an edict throughout the realm on the crimes of Zong Ben, Bingde, and the others, using Yu's accusation to substantiate it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the clerk Xiao Yu had answered as coached, Hailing proclaimed throughout the realm the crimes of Zong Ben, Bingde, and the rest, citing Yu's accusation as proof.

sentences.zh: 海陵使太府監完顏馮六籍宗本諸家，戒之曰：「珠玉金帛入於官，什器吾將分賜諸臣。」

translations.literal: Hailing had the Grand Storehouse Commissioner Wanyan Fengliu inventory the households of Zong Ben and the others, instructing him: "Pearls, jade, gold, and silk go to the state; the utensils I shall distribute among the ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing ordered Grand Storehouse Commissioner Wanyan Fengliu to inventory the estates of Zong Ben and his kin, telling him, "Pearls, jade, gold, and silk go to the treasury; the furnishings I shall distribute among my ministers."

sentences.zh: 馮六以此不復拘籍什器，往往為人持去，馮六家童亦取其檀木屏風。

translations.literal: Because of this Fengliu no longer strictly registered the utensils; they were often carried off by others, and Fengliu's household slave also took a rosewood screen.
translations.idiomatic: Fengliu therefore stopped strictly registering the furnishings, which were often carried off; even his household slave took a rosewood screen.

sentences.zh: 少監劉景前為監丞時，太府監失火，案牘盡焚毀，數月方取諸司簿帳補之，監吏坐是稽緩，當得罪。

translations.literal: The Vice Commissioner Liu Jing, when earlier serving as assistant commissioner, had seen the Grand Storehouse catch fire and all records burn; only after several months were ledgers from other offices gathered to replace them, and the clerks were slow because of this and faced punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Liu Jing, when he had served as assistant commissioner, had seen the Grand Storehouse burn and all its records destroyed; replacements were patched together from other offices' ledgers only months later, and the clerks' delay made them liable to punishment.

sentences.zh: 景為吏，倒署年月。

translations.literal: Jing, acting as a clerk, backdated the year and month.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, acting as a clerk, backdated entries in the ledgers.

sentences.zh: 太倉都監焦子忠與景有舊，坐逋負，久不得調，景為盡力出之。

translations.literal: The Grand Granary Commissioner Jiao Zizhong was an old acquaintance of Jing's; because of arrears he had long gone without promotion, and Jing did all he could to secure his release.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Granary Commissioner Jiao Zizhong was an old friend of Jing's; burdened with arrears he had long gone without promotion, and Jing worked hard to get him transferred out.

sentences.zh: 久之，馮六與景就宮中相忿爭，馮六言景倒署年月及出焦子忠事。

translations.literal: After a long while Fengliu and Jing quarreled in the palace; Fengliu spoke of Jing's backdating and securing Jiao Zizhong's release.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward Fengliu and Jing quarreled at court, and Fengliu accused Jing of backdating the ledgers and securing Jiao Zizhong's release.

sentences.zh: 禦史劾奏景，景党誘馮六家奴發盜屏事。

translations.literal: The censor memorialized against Jing; Jing's faction induced Fengliu's household slave to expose the theft of the screen.
translations.idiomatic: The censor impeached Jing; Jing's faction induced Fengliu's slave to expose the stolen screen.

sentences.zh: 馮六自陳於尚書省。

translations.literal: Fengliu made his own statement at the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Fengliu submitted his own statement to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 海陵使御史大夫趙資福、大理少卿許竑雜治。

translations.literal: Hailing had the Censor-in-Chief Zhao Zifu and the Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Hong conduct a joint investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing ordered Censor-in-Chief Zhao Zifu and Assistant Director of the Court of Judicial Review Xu Hong to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 資福等奏馮六非自盜，又嘗自首。

translations.literal: Zifu and the others memorialized that Fengliu had not stolen the goods himself and had once confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Zifu and his colleagues reported that Fengliu had not stolen the goods himself and had already made a confession.

sentences.zh: 海陵素惡馮六與宗室遊從，謂宰臣曰：「馮六嘗用所盜物，其自首不及此。

translations.literal: Hailing had long hated Fengliu for associating with the imperial clan and told the chancellors: "Fengliu once used the stolen goods; his confession did not cover this.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing had long resented Fengliu for consorting with the imperial clan. He told the chancellors, "Fengliu used the stolen goods himself; his confession did not cover that.

sentences.zh: 法，盜宮中物者死，諸物已籍入官，與宮中物何異。」

translations.literal: By law, stealing palace goods is punishable by death; all the goods had been registered into the treasury—how do they differ from palace goods?"
translations.idiomatic: The law says that stealing palace property is a capital crime. Everything had already been registered in the treasury—how is that different from palace property?"

sentences.zh: 謂馮六曰：「太府掌宮中財賄，汝當防制奸欺，而自用盜物。」

translations.literal: He told Fengliu: "The Grand Storehouse controls the palace treasury; you ought to guard against fraud, yet you yourself used stolen goods."
translations.idiomatic: He told Fengliu, "The Grand Storehouse holds the palace treasury. You were supposed to prevent fraud, yet you used stolen goods yourself."

sentences.zh: 於是，馮六棄市，資福、竑坐鞫獄不盡，決杖有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon Fengliu was executed in the marketplace; Zifu and Hong were sentenced to varying beatings for incomplete investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Fengliu was executed in the marketplace, while Zifu and Hong received beatings of varying severity for conducting an incomplete investigation.

sentences.zh: 景亦伏受焦子忠賂金。

translations.literal: Jing also confessed to accepting bribe gold from Jiao Zizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jing also confessed to taking bribe gold from Jiao Zizhong.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「受金事無左驗，景倒署年月，以免吏罪，是不可恕。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "The matter of accepting gold lacks corroborating evidence; Jing backdated the year and month to spare the clerks from punishment—this cannot be forgiven."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "There is no corroborating evidence for the bribe, but Jing backdated the ledgers to spare the clerks from punishment. That cannot be forgiven."

sentences.zh: 遂殺之。

translations.literal: He then had him killed.
translations.idiomatic: He then had him executed.

sentences.zh: 大定二年，追封宗固魯王、宗雅曹王、宗順隋王、宗懿鄭王、宗美衛王、宗哲韓王、宗本潞王、神土門豳王、斛孛束瀋王、斡烈鄂王，胡里改、胡什賚、可喜並贈金吾衛上將軍，惟宗磐、阿魯補、斛沙虎、鶻懶四人不復加封。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dading, posthumous titles were conferred: Zong Gu as Prince of Lu, Zong Ya as Prince of Cao, Zong Shun as Prince of Sui, Zong Yi as Prince of Zheng, Zong Mei as Prince of Wei, Zong Zhe as Prince of Han, Zong Ben as Prince of Lu, Shentumen as Prince of Bin, Hubosu as Prince of Shen, Wolie as Prince of E; Huligai, Hushai, and Kexi were all posthumously made generals-in-chief of the Jinwu Guard; only Zong Pan, Alubu, Hushahu, and Gulian received no further enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 2 posthumous enfeoffments were granted: Zong Gu as Prince of Lu, Zong Ya as Prince of Cao, Zong Shun as Prince of Sui, Zong Yi as Prince of Zheng, Zong Mei as Prince of Wei, Zong Zhe as Prince of Han, Zong Ben as Prince of Lu, Shentumen as Prince of Bin, Hubosu as Prince of Shen, and Wolie as Prince of E; Huligai, Hushai, and Kexi were all posthumously made generals-in-chief of the Jinwu Guard. Only Zong Pan, Alubu, Hushahu, and Gulian received no further honors.

sentences.zh: 蕭玉，奚人。

translations.literal: Xiao Yu was a Xi tribesman.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yu was a man of the Xi people.

sentences.zh: 既從蕭裕誣宗本罪，海陵喜甚，自尚書省令史為禮部尚書加特進，賜錢二千萬、馬五百匹、牛五百頭、羊千口，數月為參知政事。

translations.literal: After he followed Xiao Yu in framing Zong Ben, Hailing was greatly pleased; from a Ministry of Rites clerk he was made Minister of Rites with the extraordinary promotion, given twenty million in cash, five hundred horses, five hundred oxen, and a thousand sheep, and within months became Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After helping Xiao Yu frame Zong Ben, he won Hailing's great favor. He rose from a Ministry of Rites clerk to minister of rites with extraordinary promotion, received twenty million in cash, five hundred horses, five hundred oxen, and a thousand sheep, and within months became vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，以參政起複，俄授猛安，子尚公主。

translations.literal: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning to resume office as vice director; soon he was granted a meng'an, and his son married a princess.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he was recalled from mourning to resume office; soon he was granted a meng'an command, and his son married a princess.

sentences.zh: 海陵謂玉曰：「朕始得天下，常患太宗諸子方強，賴社稷之靈，卿發其奸。

translations.literal: Hailing told Yu: "When I first gained the realm I constantly feared Taizong's sons were still strong; relying on the state's good fortune, you exposed their treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing told Yu, "When I first seized the throne I constantly feared Taizong's sons were still powerful. Thanks to the state's good fortune, you exposed their treachery.

sentences.zh: 朕無以報此功，使朕女為卿男婦，代朕事卿也。」

translations.literal: I have no way to repay this merit; I shall give my daughter to your son in marriage, to serve you in my stead."
translations.idiomatic: I have no way to repay this service. I shall give my daughter to your son in marriage, so that she may serve you in my stead."

sentences.zh: 賜第一區，分宗本家貲賜之。

translations.literal: He bestowed one residence and divided Zong Ben's household goods to give him.
translations.idiomatic: He granted him a residence and divided Zong Ben's household goods among him as gifts.

sentences.zh: 頃之，代張浩為尚書右丞，拜平章政事，進拜右丞相，封陳國公。

translations.literal: Before long he replaced Zhang Hao as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, was appointed Director of the Secretariat, then promoted to Right Chancellor and enfeoffed as Duke of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he replaced Zhang Hao as right vice director of the Secretariat, was made director of the Secretariat, then promoted to right chancellor and enfeoffed as Duke of Chen.

sentences.zh: 文思署令閻拱與太子詹事張安妻坐奸事，獄具，不應訊而訊之。

translations.literal: Director of the Literary Bureau Yan Gong and the wife of the Crown Prince's household chief Zhang An were convicted of adultery; when the case was complete they should not have been interrogated further, yet they were.
translations.idiomatic: Literary Bureau director Yan Gong and Crown Prince household chief Zhang An's wife were convicted of adultery. Once the case was complete they should not have been interrogated further, yet they were.

sentences.zh: 海陵怒，玉與左丞蔡松年、右丞耶律安禮、禦史中丞馬諷決杖有差。

translations.literal: Hailing was angry; Yu together with Left Vice Director Cai Songnian, Right Vice Director Yelü Anli, and Censor-in-Chief Ma Feng received beatings of varying severity.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was furious. Yu, together with left vice director Cai Songnian, right vice director Yelü Anli, and censor-in-chief Ma Feng, were beaten to varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 玉等入謝罪。

translations.literal: Yu and the others entered to apologize.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and the others came in to apologize.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「為人臣以己意愛憎，妄作威福，使人畏之。

translations.literal: Hailing said: "As a minister, to act on one's own likes and dislikes and arbitrarily wield authority so that people fear one—
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "When ministers act on private likes and dislikes and arbitrarily wield authority so that people fear them—

sentences.zh: 如唐魏征、狄仁傑、姚崇、宋璟，豈肯立威使人畏哉，楊國忠之徒乃立威使人畏耳。」

translations.literal: Men like Tang's Wei Zheng, Di Renjie, Yao Chong, and Song Jing—would they establish authority to make people fear them? Only men like Yang Guozhong do that."
translations.idiomatic: Men like Tang's Wei Zheng, Di Renjie, Yao Chong, and Song Jing would never rule by fear. Only men like Yang Guozhong do that."

sentences.zh: 顧謂左司郎中吾帶、右司郎中梁球曰：「往者德宗為相，蕭斛律為左司郎中，趙德恭為右司朗中，除吏議法，多用己意。

translations.literal: He turned and told Left Department Director Wudai and Right Department Director Liang Qiu: "In the past when Dezong was chancellor, Xiao Helü was left department director and Zhao Degong was right department director; in appointing officials and deliberating law they often followed their own judgment.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to left department director Wudai and right department director Liang Qiu and said, "When Dezong was chancellor, Xiao Helü was left department director and Zhao Degong was right department director. In appointments and legal deliberation they often followed their own judgment.

sentences.zh: 汝等能不以己意愛憎為予奪輕重，不亦善乎。

translations.literal: If you can avoid letting your own likes and dislikes determine rewards, punishments, and weight of office, would that not be better?
translations.idiomatic: If you can avoid letting private likes and dislikes determine rewards, punishments, and the weight of office, would that not be better?

sentences.zh: 朕信任汝等，有過則決責之，亦非得已。

translations.literal: I trust you; when you err I have you beaten—it is not something I do willingly.
translations.idiomatic: I trust you. When you err I have you beaten, but that is not something I do willingly.

sentences.zh: 古者大臣有罪，貶謫數千里外，往來疲於奔走，有死道路者。

translations.literal: In antiquity when great ministers sinned they were exiled thousands of li away; going back and forth they were worn out with travel, and some died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity guilty ministers were exiled thousands of li away; worn out by the journey back and forth, some died on the road.

sentences.zh: 朕則不然，有過則杖之，已杖則任之如初。

translations.literal: I am not like that: when there is fault I beat them; once beaten I employ them as before.
translations.idiomatic: I am not like that. When there is fault I beat them; once beaten I employ them as before.

sentences.zh: 如有不可恕，或處之死，亦未可知。

translations.literal: If the offense is unforgivable, execution may also be possible.
translations.idiomatic: If the offense is truly unforgivable, execution may also be possible.

sentences.zh: 汝等自勉。」

translations.literal: Exert yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Exert yourselves."

sentences.zh: 正隆三年，拜司徒，判大宗正事。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenglong he was appointed Grand Mentor and concurrently Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenglong 3 he was appointed grand mentor and concurrently director of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 五年，玉以司徒兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Yu served as Grand Mentor and concurrently Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Yu served as grand mentor and concurrently censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 使參知政事李通諭旨曰：「判宗正之職固重，御史大夫尤難其人。

translations.literal: He had Vice Director Li Tong convey the instruction: "The post of Director of the Imperial Clan is weighty in itself, but the censor-in-chief is especially hard to find a fit man for.
translations.idiomatic: He had vice director Li Tong convey the instruction: "The post of director of the imperial clan is weighty in itself, but finding a fit censor-in-chief is especially difficult.

sentences.zh: 朕將行幸南京，官吏多不法受賕，卿宜專糾劾，細務非所責也。

translations.literal: I am about to travel to Nanjing; many officials there unlawfully accept bribes—you should focus on impeachment; minor matters are not your charge.
translations.idiomatic: I am about to travel to Nanjing, where many officials unlawfully accept bribes. You should focus on impeachment; minor matters are not your charge.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫與宰執不相遠，朕至南京，徐當思之。」

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief is not far from the chancellors; when I reach Nanjing I shall consider the matter further."
translations.idiomatic: The censor-in-chief is not far removed from the chancellors. When I reach Nanjing I shall consider the matter further."

sentences.zh: 繼以司徒判大興尹，玉固辭司徒。

translations.literal: He then had him as Grand Mentor concurrently prefect of Daxing; Yu firmly declined the Grand Mentor post.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed him grand mentor and concurrently prefect of Daxing; Yu firmly declined the grand mentor post.

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「朕將南巡，京師地重，非大臣不能鎮撫，留卿居守，無為多讓。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "I am about to tour the south; the capital's territory is weighty and only a great minister can pacify it—remain to guard it, do not decline too much."
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "I am about to tour the south. The capital is too important for anyone but a great minister to hold. Remain and guard it; do not decline so much."

sentences.zh: 海陵至南京，以玉為尚書左丞相，進封吳國公。

translations.literal: When Hailing reached Nanjing he made Yu Left Chancellor and advanced his enfeoffment to Duke of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing reached Nanjing he made Yu left chancellor and advanced his enfeoffment to Duke of Wu.

sentences.zh: 海陵將伐宋，因賜群臣宴，顧謂玉曰：「卿嘗讀書否？」

translations.literal: As Hailing was about to attack Song he gave a feast to the ministers and turned to Yu: "Have you ever read books?"
translations.idiomatic: As Hailing was about to attack Song he gave a feast for the ministers and asked Yu, "Have you ever read books?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「亦嘗觀之。」

translations.literal: He replied: "I have looked at them."
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "I have looked at them."

sentences.zh: 中宴，海陵起，即召玉至內閤，因以《漢書》一冊示玉。

translations.literal: Mid-feast Hailing rose and at once summoned Yu to the inner chamber, showing him one volume of the "Book of Han."
translations.idiomatic: Midway through the feast Hailing rose and summoned Yu to the inner chamber, showing him one volume of the Book of Han.

sentences.zh: 既而擲之曰：「此非所問也，朕欲與卿議事。

translations.literal: Then he threw it down and said: "That is not what I am asking; I wish to discuss affairs with you.
translations.idiomatic: Then he threw it aside and said, "That is not what I am asking. I wish to discuss affairs with you.

sentences.zh: 朕今欲伐江南，卿以為如何？」

translations.literal: I now wish to attack Jiangnan—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: I now wish to attack Jiangnan. What do you think?"

sentences.zh: 玉對曰：「不可。」

translations.literal: Yu replied: "It cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "It cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 海陵曰：「朕視宋國猶掌握間耳，何為不可。」

translations.literal: Hailing said: "I regard the Song state as within my grasp—why can it not be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Hailing said, "I regard the Song as within my grasp. Why can it not be done?"

sentences.zh: 玉曰：「天以長江限南北，舟楫非我所長。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Heaven uses the Yangtze to divide north and south; boats and oars are not our strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Heaven uses the Yangtze to divide north and south. Boats and oars are not our strength.

sentences.zh: 苻堅百萬伐晉，不能以一騎渡，以是知其不可。」

translations.literal: Fu Jian with a million men attacked Jin and could not get a single rider across—by this one knows it cannot be done."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian attacked Jin with a million men and could not get a single rider across the river. That shows it cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 海陵怒，叱之使出。

translations.literal: Hailing was angry and shouted him out.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing was furious and shouted him out.

sentences.zh: 及張浩因周福兒附奏，海陵杖張浩，並杖玉。

translations.literal: When Zhang Hao submitted a memorial through Zhou Fu'er, Hailing beat Zhang Hao and also beat Yu.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hao submitted a memorial through Zhou Fu'er, Hailing beat Zhang Hao and beat Yu as well.

sentences.zh: 因謂群臣曰：「浩大臣，不面奏，因人達語，輕易如此。

translations.literal: He then told the ministers: "Hao is a great minister; instead of memorializing in person he sent words through another—how lightly he treats this.
translations.idiomatic: He then told the ministers, "Hao is a great minister. Instead of memorializing in person he sent words through another person. How lightly he treats his duty.

sentences.zh: 玉以苻堅比朕，朕欲斷其舌，釘而礫之，以玉有功，隱忍至今。

translations.literal: Yu compared me to Fu Jian; I wished to cut out his tongue, nail him, and crush him to bits—for Yu's merit I have restrained myself until now.
translations.idiomatic: Yu compared me to Fu Jian. I wanted to cut out his tongue, nail him up, and crush him to bits. For Yu's past merit I have restrained myself until now.

sentences.zh: 大臣決責，痛及爾體，如在朕躬，有不能已者，汝等悉之。」

translations.literal: When great ministers are beaten the pain reaches your bodies as if it were my own—I cannot always restrain myself; you all understand this."
translations.idiomatic: When great ministers are beaten the pain reaches your bodies as if it were my own. I cannot always restrain myself. You all understand this."

sentences.zh: 及海陵自將發南京，玉與張浩留治省事。

translations.literal: When Hailing personally led the army out from Nanjing, Yu and Zhang Hao remained to handle routine business.
translations.idiomatic: When Hailing personally led the army out from Nanjing, Yu and Zhang Hao remained behind to handle routine business.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，降奉國上將軍，放歸田里，奪所賜家產。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne Yu was reduced to General-in-Chief Who Upholds the State, released to his home district, and stripped of all granted property.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong took the throne Yu was reduced to general-in-chief who upholds the state, sent home, and stripped of all granted property.

sentences.zh: 久之，起為孟州防禦使。

translations.literal: After a long while he was recalled as defense commissioner of Mengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was recalled as defense commissioner of Mengzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗戒之曰：「昔海陵欲殺太宗子孫，借汝為證，遂被進用。

translations.literal: Shizong admonished him: "In the past Hailing wished to kill Taizong's descendants and used you as witness, and so you were advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong admonished him: "In the past Hailing wished to kill Taizong's descendants and used you as witness, and so you were advanced.

sentences.zh: 朕思海陵肆虐，先殺宗本諸人，然後用汝質成其事，豈得專罪汝等。

translations.literal: I consider that Hailing acted tyrannically, first killing Zong Ben and the others and then using you to substantiate the case—how can the blame fall on you alone?
translations.idiomatic: I consider that Hailing acted tyrannically, first killing Zong Ben and the others and then using you to substantiate the case. How can the blame fall on you alone?

sentences.zh: 今複用汝，當思改過。

translations.literal: Now that I employ you again, you must think to reform.
translations.idiomatic: Now that I employ you again, you must think to reform.

sentences.zh: 若謂嘗居要地，以今日為不足，必罰無赦。」

translations.literal: If you think that because you once held high office today's post is beneath you, punishment will be without pardon."
translations.idiomatic: If you think that because you once held high office today's post is beneath you, punishment will be without pardon."

sentences.zh: 轉定海軍節度使，改太原尹，與少尹烏古論掃喝互訟不公事，各削一官，解職，尋卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military commissioner of Dinghai, then made prefect of Taiyuan; he and Vice Prefect Wugulun Saohe sued each other over unfair dealings, each was reduced one rank and dismissed, and soon he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military commissioner of Dinghai, then made prefect of Taiyuan. He and vice prefect Wugulun Saohe sued each other over unfair dealings; each was reduced one rank and dismissed, and soon he died.

sentences.zh: 子德用。

translations.literal: Son: Deyong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Deyong.

sentences.zh: 大定二十四年，尚書省奏玉子德用當升除，上曰：「海陵假口於玉以快其毒，玉子豈可升除邪。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Dading the Ministry of Rites memorialized that Yu's son Deyong should be promoted; the emperor said: "Hailing used Yu as a mouthpiece to satisfy his cruelty—how can Yu's son be promoted?"
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 24 the Ministry of Rites memorialized that Yu's son Deyong should be promoted. The emperor said, "Hailing used Yu as a mouthpiece to satisfy his cruelty. How can Yu's son be promoted?"

sentences.zh: 贊曰：宗磐嘗從斜也取中京，不可謂無勞伐者，世祿鮮禮，自古有之，在國家善為保全之道耳。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Zong Pan once followed Xieye in taking the Central Capital and cannot be said to have lacked merit in the campaigns; hereditary stipends rarely preserve ritual propriety—this has been so since antiquity; what matters is that the state know how to preserve them properly.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: Zong Pan once followed Xieye in taking the Central Capital and cannot be said to have lacked merit in the campaigns. Hereditary stipends rarely preserve ritual propriety—this has been so since antiquity. What matters is that the state know how to preserve them properly.

sentences.zh: 熙宗殺宗磐而存恤其母后，雖雲矯情，猶畏物論。

translations.literal: Xizong killed Zong Pan yet preserved and comforted his mother the empress dowager; though one may say this was feigned feeling, he still feared public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Xizong killed Zong Pan yet preserved and comforted his mother the empress dowager. Though one may call this feigned feeling, he still feared public opinion.

sentences.zh: 海陵造謀，殺宗本兄弟不遺餘力。

translations.literal: Hailing devised the plot and killed Zong Ben and his brothers without sparing any effort.
translations.idiomatic: Hailing devised the plot and killed Zong Ben and his brothers without sparing any effort.

sentences.zh: 太宗舉宋而有中原，金百世不遷之廟也，再傳而無噍類，於是太祖之美意無複幾微存者。

translations.literal: Taizong raised the army against Song and gained the Central Plains—the temple that Jin would not move for a hundred generations; after two transmissions not a mouthful remained, and thus the Grand Ancestor's fine intent scarcely survived at all.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong raised the army against Song and gained the Central Plains—the temple Jin would not move for a hundred generations. After two transmissions not a mouthful remained, and the Grand Ancestor's fine intent scarcely survived at all.

sentences.zh: 春秋之世，宋公舍與夷而立其弟，禍延數世，害及五國，誠足為後世監乎。

translations.literal: In the age of the Spring and Autumn Annals Duke Huan of Song set aside his son Yifu and established his younger brother; disaster extended for generations and harm reached five states—truly enough to serve as a warning for later ages.
translations.idiomatic: In the Spring and Autumn era Duke Huan of Song set aside his son Yifu and established his younger brother. Disaster extended for generations and harm reached five states—truly enough to serve as a warning for later ages.

sentences.zh: 杲本名斜也，世祖第五子，太祖母弟。

translations.literal: Gao's original name was Xieye; he was the fifth son of Shizu and younger brother of the Grand Empress.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was born Xieye, the fifth son of Shizu and younger brother of the Grand Empress.

sentences.zh: 收國元年，太宗為諳班勃極烈，杲為國論吳勃極烈。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shouguo, Taizong was anban bojilie and Gao was guolun wu bojilie.
translations.idiomatic: In Shouguo 1 Taizong was anban bojilie and Gao was guolun wu bojilie.

sentences.zh: 天輔元年，杲以兵一萬攻泰州，下金山縣，女固、脾室四部及渤海人皆來降，遂克泰州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianfu, Gao with ten thousand troops attacked Taizhou, took Jinshan County; the Nügu, Pishi four tribes and Bohai people all came to surrender, and he then captured Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 1 Gao led ten thousand troops against Taizhou and took Jinshan County. The Nügu, Pishi four tribes, and Bohai people all surrendered, and he then captured Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 城中積粟轉致烏林野，賑先降諸部，因徙之內地。

translations.literal: The grain stored in the city was transported to the Wulin wilds; he relieved the tribes that had surrendered first and then moved them into the interior.
translations.idiomatic: The grain stored in the city was transported to the Wulin wilds. He relieved the tribes that had surrendered first and then moved them into the interior.

sentences.zh: 天輔五年，為忽魯勃極烈，都統內外諸軍，取中京實北京也，蒲家奴、宗翰、宗幹、宗磐副之，宗峻領合紮猛安，皆受金牌，耶律餘睹為鄉導。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu he became hulu bojilie, commander-in-chief of all armies inside and outside; taking the Central Capital was in fact taking the Northern Capital. Pujianu, Zong Han, Zong Gan, and Zong Pan assisted him; Zong Jun led the combined meng'an; all received gold plaques; Yelü Yudu served as guide.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 5 he became hulu bojilie and commander-in-chief of all armies inside and outside. Taking the Central Capital was in fact taking the Northern Capital. Pujianu, Zong Han, Zong Gan, and Zong Pan assisted him; Zong Jun led the combined meng'an; all received gold plaques; Yelü Yudu served as guide.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「遼政不綱，人神共棄。

translations.literal: The edict said: "Liao government lacks discipline; men and spirits alike have abandoned it.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "Liao government lacks discipline. Men and spirits alike have abandoned it.

sentences.zh: 今欲中外一統，故命汝率大軍，以行討伐。

translations.literal: Now I wish to unify inside and outside, and therefore command you to lead a great army to conduct the punitive campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to unify inside and outside, and therefore command you to lead a great army on the punitive campaign.

sentences.zh: 爾其慎重兵事，擇用善謀。

translations.literal: You must be careful in military affairs and choose good stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: You must be careful in military affairs and choose good stratagems.

sentences.zh: 賞罰必行，糧餉必繼。

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments must be carried out; provisions must be continuously supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and punishments must be carried out, and provisions must be continuously supplied.

sentences.zh: 勿擾降服，勿縱俘掠。

translations.literal: Do not disturb those who surrender; do not allow plunder of captives.
translations.idiomatic: Do not disturb those who surrender, and do not allow plunder of captives.

sentences.zh: 見可而進，無淹師期。

translations.literal: Advance when you see opportunity; do not delay the campaign beyond its term.
translations.idiomatic: Advance when you see opportunity, and do not delay the campaign beyond its term.

sentences.zh: 事有從權，毋煩奏稟。」

translations.literal: When affairs permit discretion, do not trouble me with memorials."
translations.idiomatic: When affairs permit discretion, do not trouble me with memorials."

sentences.zh: 複詔曰：「若克中京，所得禮樂圖書文籍，並先次律發赴闕。」

translations.literal: Another edict said: "If you capture the Central Capital, the ritual objects, music, books, and records obtained—send them first in order to the court."
translations.idiomatic: Another edict said, "If you capture the Central Capital, send the ritual objects, music, books, and records obtained to the court in order of priority."

sentences.zh: 當是時，遼人守中京者，聞知師期，焚芻糧，欲徙居民遁去。

translations.literal: At that time the Liao defenders of the Central Capital, hearing the date of the campaign, burned fodder and grain and wished to move the inhabitants away and flee.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Liao defenders of the Central Capital, hearing the date of the campaign, burned fodder and grain and wished to move the inhabitants away and flee.

sentences.zh: 奚王霞未則欲視我兵少則迎戰，若不敵則退保山西。

translations.literal: The Xi Prince Xia Mo wished to see whether our troops were few and then give battle; if not a match he would retreat and hold the western mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi Prince Xia Mo wished to see whether our troops were few and then give battle; if not a match he would retreat and hold the western mountains.

sentences.zh: 杲知遼人無鬥志，乃委輜重，以輕兵擊之。

translations.literal: Gao knew the Liao had no fighting spirit; he therefore left the baggage train and struck with light troops.
translations.idiomatic: Gao knew the Liao had no fighting spirit. He therefore left the baggage train and struck with light troops.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，克高、恩回紇三城，進至中京。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year he captured the three cities of Gao, En, and Huihe, and advanced to the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year he captured the three cities of Gao, En, and Huihe and advanced to the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 遼兵皆不戰而潰，遂克中京。

translations.literal: The Liao troops all fled without fighting, and he then captured the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao troops all fled without fighting, and he then captured the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 獲馬一千二百、牛五百、駝一百七十、羊四萬七千、車三百五十兩。

translations.literal: He obtained twelve hundred horses, five hundred oxen, one hundred seventy camels, forty-seven thousand sheep, and three hundred fifty carts.
translations.idiomatic: He obtained twelve hundred horses, five hundred oxen, one hundred seventy camels, forty-seven thousand sheep, and three hundred fifty carts.

sentences.zh: 乃分兵屯守要害之地。

translations.literal: He then divided troops to garrison strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: He then divided troops to garrison strategic points.

sentences.zh: 駐兵中京，使使奏捷、獻俘。

translations.literal: He encamped at the Central Capital and sent envoys to report victory and present captives.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at the Central Capital and sent envoys to report victory and present captives.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「汝等提兵於外，克副所任，攻下城邑，撫安人民，朕甚嘉之。

translations.literal: The edict said: "You who lead troops abroad have fulfilled your charge, taken cities, and pacified the people—I greatly commend this.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "You who lead troops abroad have fulfilled your charge, taken cities, and pacified the people. I greatly commend this.

sentences.zh: 分遣將士招降山前諸部，計已撫定。

translations.literal: Dispatch generals and soldiers to induce the mountain-front tribes to surrender—the plan is already to pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch generals and soldiers to induce the mountain-front tribes to surrender. The plan is already to pacify them.

sentences.zh: 山后若未可往，即營田牧，俟秋大舉，更當熟議，見可則行。

translations.literal: If the area beyond the mountains is not yet accessible, then farm and herd and wait until autumn for a major campaign; deliberate further then, and act when you see opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: If the area beyond the mountains is not yet accessible, then farm and herd and wait until autumn for a major campaign. Deliberate further then, and act when you see opportunity.

sentences.zh: 如欲益兵，具數來上。

translations.literal: If you wish to increase troops, report the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to increase troops, report the numbers.

sentences.zh: 無恃一戰之勝，輒自弛慢。

translations.literal: Do not rely on the victory of a single battle and grow slack on your own.
translations.idiomatic: Do not rely on the victory of a single battle and grow slack on your own.

sentences.zh: 善撫存降附，宣諭將士，使知朕意。」

translations.literal: Treat surrendered and attached peoples well; proclaim to the generals and soldiers so they know my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Treat surrendered and attached peoples well. Proclaim to the generals and soldiers so they know my intent."

sentences.zh: 完顏歡都遊兵出中京南，遇騎兵三十餘紿曰：「乞明旦來降於此。」

translations.literal: Wanyan Huandu's raiding troops went out south of the Central Capital and encountered more than thirty horsemen who deceived them, saying: "Beg to come surrender here tomorrow morning."
translations.idiomatic: Wanyan Huandu's raiding troops went out south of the Central Capital and encountered more than thirty horsemen who deceived them, saying, "We beg to come surrender here tomorrow morning."

sentences.zh: 杲信之，使溫蒂痕阿里出、納合鈍恩、蒲察婆羅偎、諸甲拔剔鄰往迎之。

translations.literal: Gao believed them and sent Wendihen Ali Chu, Nahe Dun'en, Pucha Poluowei, and Zhujia Batiji to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao believed them and sent Wendihen Ali Chu, Nahe Dun'en, Pucha Poluowei, and Zhujia Batiji to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 奚王霞末兵圍阿里出等。

translations.literal: The Xi Prince Xia Mo's troops surrounded Ali Chu and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi Prince Xia Mo's troops surrounded Ali Chu and the others.

sentences.zh: 遂據阪去馬，皆殊死戰，敗霞末兵，追殺至暮而還。

translations.literal: They then dismounted on the slope; all fought to the death, defeated Xia Mo's troops, and pursued until evening before returning.
translations.idiomatic: They then dismounted on the slope. All fought to the death, defeated Xia Mo's troops, and pursued until evening before returning.

sentences.zh: 是役，納合鈍恩功為多。

translations.literal: In this battle Nahe Dun'en's merit was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In this battle Nahe Dun'en's merit was greatest.

sentences.zh: 宗翰降北安州，希尹獲遼護衛習泥烈，言遼主在鴛鴦濼畋獵，可襲取之。

translations.literal: Zong Han reduced Bei'an Prefecture; Xiyin captured the Liao guard Xini Lie, who said the Liao sovereign was hunting at Yuanyang Marsh and could be taken in a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han reduced Bei'an Prefecture. Xiyin captured the Liao guard Xini Lie, who said the Liao sovereign was hunting at Yuanyang Marsh and could be taken in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 宗翰移書於杲，請進兵。

translations.literal: Zong Han sent a letter to Gao requesting advance of the army.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han sent a letter to Gao requesting advance of the army.

sentences.zh: 使者再往，曰：「一失機會，事難圖矣。」

translations.literal: The envoy came a second time, saying: "Once opportunity is lost the affair is hard to accomplish."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy came a second time, saying, "Once opportunity is lost the affair is hard to accomplish."

sentences.zh: 杲意尚未決。

translations.literal: Gao's mind was not yet decided.
translations.idiomatic: Gao's mind was not yet made up.

sentences.zh: 宗幹勸杲當從宗翰策，杲乃約宗翰會奚王嶺。

translations.literal: Zong Gan urged Gao to follow Zong Han's plan; Gao then arranged to meet Zong Han at the Xi Prince's Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Gan urged Gao to follow Zong Han's plan. Gao then arranged to meet Zong Han at the Xi Prince's Ridge.

sentences.zh: 既會，始定議，杲出青嶺，宗翰出瓢嶺，期羊城濼會軍。

translations.literal: Once they met they settled the plan: Gao would go out by the Green Ridge and Zong Han by the Gourd Ridge, agreeing to join forces at Yangcheng Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: Once they met they settled the plan: Gao would advance by the Green Ridge and Zong Han by the Gourd Ridge, agreeing to join forces at Yangcheng Marsh.

sentences.zh: 時遼主在草濼，使宗翰與宗幹率精兵六千襲之。

translations.literal: At that time the Liao sovereign was at Caomarsh; he ordered Zong Han and Zong Gan to lead six thousand picked troops in a surprise attack.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Liao sovereign was at Caomarsh. He ordered Zong Han and Zong Gan to lead six thousand picked troops in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 遼主西走，其都統馬哥趨搗里。

translations.literal: The Liao sovereign fled west; his commander-in-chief Mage rushed toward Daoli.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao sovereign fled west, while his commander-in-chief Mage rushed toward Daoli.

sentences.zh: 宗翰遣撻懶以兵一千往擊之。

translations.literal: Zong Han sent Tadan with a thousand troops to strike him.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Han sent Tadan with a thousand troops to strike him.

sentences.zh: 撻懶請益兵於都統杲，而獲遼樞密使得里底父子。

translations.literal: Tadan requested reinforcements from Commander-in-Chief Gao and captured the Liao Privy Councilor Delidi and his son.
translations.idiomatic: Tadan requested reinforcements from Commander-in-Chief Gao and captured the Liao privy councilor Delidi and his son.

sentences.zh: 西京已降得叛，杲使招之不從，遂攻之。

translations.literal: The Western Capital had already surrendered to Dede; Gao sent to summon him but he would not come, and so attacked.
translations.idiomatic: The Western Capital had already surrendered to Dede. Gao sent to summon him but he would not come, and so attacked.

sentences.zh: 留守蕭察刺逾城降。

translations.literal: The defending prefect Xiao Chaci leaped over the wall and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The defending prefect Xiao Chaci leaped over the wall and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 四月，複取西京。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he again took the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he again took the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 杲率大軍趨白水濼，分遣諸將招撫未降州郡及諸部族。

translations.literal: Gao led the great army toward Baishui Marsh and dispatched the generals to induce the unsubdued prefectures and various tribes to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Gao led the great army toward Baishui Marsh and dispatched generals to induce unsubdued prefectures and various tribes to submit.

sentences.zh: 於是，遼秦晉國王耶律捏里自立於燕京。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Liao Qin-Jin Prince Yelü Nieli declared himself sovereign at Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Liao Qin-Jin Prince Yelü Nieli declared himself sovereign at Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 山西諸城雖降，而人心未固，杲遣宗望奏事，仍請上臨軍。

translations.literal: The cities of the western mountains had surrendered but hearts were not yet firm; Gao sent Zong Wang to memorialize and still requested that the sovereign come in person to the army.
translations.idiomatic: The cities of the western mountains had surrendered but hearts were not yet firm. Gao sent Zong Wang to memorialize and still requested that the sovereign come in person to the army.

sentences.zh: 耶律坦招西南招討司及所屬諸部，西至夏境皆降，耶律佛頂亦降於坦。

translations.literal: Yelü Tan induced the Southwest Pacification Commission and its subordinate tribes; west to the Xia border all surrendered, and Yelü Foding also surrendered to Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Tan induced the Southwest Pacification Commission and its subordinate tribes. West to the Xia border all surrendered, and Yelü Foding also surrendered to Tan.

sentences.zh: 金肅、西平二郡漢軍四千叛去，坦與阿沙兀野、撻不野簡料新降丁壯，迨夜襲之。

translations.literal: The four thousand Han troops of Jin Su and Xiping prefectures rebelled and fled; Tan with Ashuwuye and Tabuye selected newly surrendered strong youths and at night raided them.
translations.idiomatic: Four thousand Han troops of Jin Su and Xiping prefectures rebelled and fled. Tan with Ashuwuye and Tabuye selected newly surrendered strong youths and raided them at night.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，戰於河上，大敗其眾，皆委仗就擒。

translations.literal: At dawn they fought on the river, greatly defeated their force, and all cast aside weapons and were captured.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn they fought on the river, greatly defeated their force, and all cast aside weapons and were captured.

sentences.zh: 耶律捏里移書於杲請和，杲複書，責以不先稟命上國，輒稱大號，若能自歸，當以燕京留守處之。

translations.literal: Yelü Nieli sent a letter to Gao seeking peace; Gao replied, rebuking him for not first reporting to the suzerain state and rashly assuming the great title—if he would submit of himself he would be given the post of Yanjing prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Yelü Nieli sent a letter to Gao seeking peace. Gao replied, rebuking him for not first reporting to the suzerain state and rashly assuming the great title—if he would submit of himself he would be given the post of Yanjing prefect.

sentences.zh: 捏里複以書來，其略曰：「昨即位時，在兩國絕聘交兵之際。

translations.literal: Nieli sent another letter, the gist of which was: "When I first took the throne it was at a time when the two states had broken off embassies and were at war.
translations.idiomatic: Nieli sent another letter, the gist of which was: "When I first took the throne it was at a time when the two states had broken off embassies and were at war.

sentences.zh: 奚王與文武百官同心推戴，何暇請命。

translations.literal: The Xi Prince and the civil and military officials all pushed me together—how could I spare time to request permission?
translations.idiomatic: The Xi Prince and the civil and military officials all pushed me together—how could I spare time to request permission?

sentences.zh: 今諸軍已集，儻欲加兵，未能束手待斃也。

translations.literal: Now the armies have gathered; if you wish to add troops I cannot wait with bound hands to perish.
translations.idiomatic: Now the armies have gathered. If you wish to add troops I cannot wait with bound hands to perish.

sentences.zh: 昔我先世，未嘗殘害大金人民，寵以位呈，日益強大。

translations.literal: In the past my forebears never harmed the people of Great Jin but favored them with offices, and day by day we grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: In the past my forebears never harmed the people of Great Jin but favored them with offices, and day by day we grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 今忘此施，欲絕我宗祀，於義何如也。

translations.literal: Now forgetting this kindness you wish to cut off my ancestral sacrifices—how is this righteous?
translations.idiomatic: Now forgetting this kindness you wish to cut off my ancestral sacrifices—how is this righteous?

sentences.zh: 儻蒙惠顧，則感戴恩德，何有窮已。」

translations.literal: If you would show favor I would be grateful for your grace without end."
translations.idiomatic: If you would show favor I would be grateful for your grace without end."

sentences.zh: 杲複書曰L：「閤下向為元帥，總統諸軍，任非不重，竟無尺寸之功。

translations.literal: Gao replied: "Your Excellency formerly served as commander-in-chief, directing all armies—your charge was not light, yet in the end you achieved not the slightest merit.
translations.idiomatic: Gao replied, "Your Excellency formerly served as commander-in-chief directing all armies. Your charge was not light, yet in the end you achieved not the slightest merit.

sentences.zh: 欲據一城，以抗國兵，不亦難乎。

translations.literal: To hold one city and resist the state's army—is that not difficult?
translations.idiomatic: To hold one city and resist the state's army—is that not difficult?

sentences.zh: 所任用者，前既不能死國，今誰肯為閤下用者。

translations.literal: Those you employ—before they could not die for the state; now who would be willing to serve Your Excellency?
translations.idiomatic: Those you employ—before they could not die for the state. Now who would be willing to serve Your Excellency?

sentences.zh: 而雲主辱臣死，欲恃此以成功，計亦疏矣。

translations.literal: Yet you say the sovereign insults ministers unto death and wish to rely on this to succeed—the plan is also crude.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you say the sovereign insults ministers unto death and wish to rely on this to succeed—the plan is also crude.

sentences.zh: 幕府奉詔，歸者官之，逆者討之。

translations.literal: The headquarters follows the edict: those who submit receive office; those who resist are punished.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters follows the edict: those who submit receive office; those who resist are punished.

sentences.zh: 若執迷不從，期於殄滅而後已。」

translations.literal: If you cling obstinately and do not follow, the term is set for extermination afterward."
translations.idiomatic: If you cling obstinately and do not follow, the term is set for extermination afterward."

sentences.zh: 捏里乃遣使請于太祖。

translations.literal: Nieli then sent envoys to request terms of the Grand Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Nieli then sent envoys to request terms of the Grand Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 賜捏里詔曰：「汝，遼之所屬，位居將相，不能與國存亡，乃竊據孤城，僭稱大號，若不降附，將有後悔。」

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor bestowed an edict on Nieli: "You belong to Liao, hold the rank of general and chancellor, yet cannot live or die with the state; you usurp an isolated city and presumptuously assume the great title—if you do not submit and attach yourself there will be regret afterward."
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor bestowed an edict on Nieli: "You belong to Liao, hold the rank of general and chancellor, yet cannot live or die with the state. You usurp an isolated city and presumptuously assume the great title. If you do not submit there will be regret afterward."

sentences.zh: 六月，上發京師，詔都統曰：「汝等欲朕親征，已於今月朔旦啟行。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the sovereign set out from the capital and issued an edict the commander-in-chief: "You wished me to campaign in person; I have already set out on the first day of this month.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the sovereign set out from the capital and issued an edict the commander-in-chief: "You wished me to campaign in person. I have already set out on the first day of this month.

sentences.zh: 遼主今定何在？

translations.literal: Where is the Liao sovereign now fixed?
translations.idiomatic: Where is the Liao sovereign now?

sentences.zh: 何計可以取之，其具以聞。」

translations.literal: What plan can take him? Report in full."
translations.idiomatic: What plan can take him? Report in full."

sentences.zh: 杲使馬和尚奉迎太祖于撻魯河。

translations.literal: Gao had the monk Mashang welcome the Grand Ancestor at the Talu River.
translations.idiomatic: Gao had the monk Mashang welcome the Grand Ancestor at the Talu River.

sentences.zh: 斡魯、婁室敗夏將李良輔，杲使完顏希尹等奏捷，且請徙西南招討司諸部於內地。

translations.literal: Wolu and Nianshi defeated the Xia general Li Liangfu; Gao had Wanyan Xiyin and others memorialize the victory and request moving the Southwest Pacification Commission tribes into the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Wolu and Nianshi defeated the Xia general Li Liangfu. Gao had Wanyan Xiyin and others memorialize the victory and request moving the Southwest Pacification Commission tribes into the interior.

sentences.zh: 希尹等見上於大濼西南，上嘉賞之。

translations.literal: Xiyin and the others saw the sovereign southwest of the Great Marsh; the sovereign commended and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyin and the others saw the sovereign southwest of the Great Marsh. The sovereign commended and rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 上至鴛鴦濼，杲上謁。

translations.literal: When the sovereign reached Yuanyang Marsh, Gao paid his respects.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign reached Yuanyang Marsh, Gao paid his respects.

sentences.zh: 上追遼主至回離畛川，南伐燕京，次奉聖州。

translations.literal: The sovereign pursued the Liao sovereign to the Huili Ridge River, then campaigned south against Yanjing, halting at Fengsheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign pursued the Liao sovereign to the Huili Ridge River, then campaigned south against Yanjing, halting at Fengsheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「自今諸訴訟書付都統杲決遣。

translations.literal: The edict said: "From now on all litigation documents are entrusted to Commander-in-Chief Gao for decision.
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "From now on all litigation documents are entrusted to Commander-in-Chief Gao for decision.

sentences.zh: 若有大疑，即令聞奏。」

translations.literal: If there is great doubt, then have it reported."
translations.idiomatic: If there is great doubt, then have it reported."

sentences.zh: 太祖定燕京，還次鴛鴦濼，以宗翰為都統，杲從上還京師。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor settled Yanjing, returned and halted at Yuanyang Marsh, made Zong Han commander-in-chief, and Gao followed the sovereign back to the capital.
